witnesses.provenance: Solana's per-transaction MAX_COMPUTE_UNIT_LIMIT is 1,400,000 compute units. It is the chain's limit, not ours. The campaign sets ProgramTest's ceiling to exactly that value and never raises it -- the test itself asserts every one of the four commit CUs against this same bound.

Solana's legacy packet maximum is 1,232 bytes (PACKET_DATA_BYTES). ProgramTest submits no packet and cannot enforce it, so a frame past the limit survives a fast lane untouched -- Found31 was ten bytes over and survived every fixture test in the tree. This campaign therefore serialises every transaction it submits over a real activated Address Lookup Table and records the extent, and this witness checks the largest against the stated limit.
A `wire_bytes` of null says the campaign did not measure, which is honest but is not a claim that the frame fits. This asserts that no transaction in this campaign is unmeasured.

witnesses.query: [.transactions[] | select(.error != null) | select([.logs[] | select(contains("custom program error: 0x"))] | length == 0)] | length | tostring
witnesses.provenance: The Solana runtime reports a privilege, frame, or account refusal it decides ITSELF as a bare InstructionError with no `custom program error:` log line; that line appears only when a program returned ProgramError::Custom. Every refusal this campaign claims -- named or unnamed_refusal -- is a program decision, so a bare runtime refusal appearing here would mean a hostile case stopped being about a program.

witnesses.provenance: A rollback case is only evidence if the thing being rolled back actually happened. This asserts, from the runtime's own log, that each of the four late-refusal transactions the ledger records as FAILED contains at least one completed Claims invocation (E3M3d7sy8ZKivUGxBexL9wxE7ebqzGWFqkdeFMedCJFS is the claims program address pinned in tools/gauntlet/claims-rational-lifecycle/programs.json).
